title: Telling what happened
job: A four-sentence account in the past
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: TWO PASTS, TWO JOBS. The imparfait paints the standing situation a story happens against — what was already going on, what things were like, the weather, a habit, an age. The passé composé moves the account forward one completed step at a time. Il était tard et il n'y avait personne. Alors j'ai appelé Anne. L1-M5 shipped the second and never taught the choice; this is where it is taught.

THE SLOGAN TO KILL: "one is for completed actions and the other for ongoing ones". It breaks on the first real account. Hier j'ai mangé à sept heures is completed. Je mangeais quand tu as appelé is not "ongoing" in any objective sense — it is background for the call. Quand j'étais petit, j'allais toujours à la mer is a habit and not a duration. What decides it is the ROLE the clause plays in the telling.

THE AUXILIARY LAW, written down at last: être for the movement and change-of-state verbs — aller, venir, partir, rester, rentrer, arriver — and for reflexives, with the participle agreeing with the SUBJECT in gender and number. avoir for everything else, with no agreement at all. L1 taught the agreement by example in allée and restée; here is the rule behind it.

The sequencers are the honest new spend: d'abord, ensuite and enfin, beside L1-M10's puis, et puis and alors. Each account is four short sentences rather than one long one, and almost every word in them comes from L1 and from M1–M9.

Nothing new is opened. The plus-que-parfait, the subjunctive, the conditional beyond M1's frozen je voudrais, and reported speech all stay OUT and belong to L3 — which is why an account here reports what happened and never what anyone said about it.

sentences.display: Il était tard. Il n'y avait personne. Alors j'ai appelé Anne
sentences.cue: It was late. There was nobody. So I called Anne
sentences.literal: It was late. It not-there had nobody. So I-have called Anne

words.note: The imparfait of être. It says what things were LIKE and does not move the story on — which is the whole of what the tense does.
L1-M7's il y a in the imparfait, and one whole surface as that one is. It covers both English numbers.
With ne in front of the verb it means nobody; on its own it is a person. The negative reading needs that ne and cannot do without it.
The d is silent. Il est tard is late in the day; en retard is late for something, and the two are not swapped.

sentences.trap: Two imparfaits set the scene and one passé composé moves it. That is the whole architecture of a French account, visible in three short sentences.
sentences.sound: ee-lay-TAR. eel nya-VAY per-SON. a-LOR zhay a-puh-LAY AN. The imparfait endings all run to the same -ait sound.

variations.display: Il était tard. Alors j'ai appelé Anne
variations.cue: It was late. So I called Anne
variations.changed: two steps instead of three

variations.display: Il n'y avait personne. Alors je suis rentré
variations.cue: There was nobody. So I went home
variations.changed: movement, so être and an agreeing participle

variations.display: Il était tard et il n'y avait personne
variations.cue: It was late and there was nobody
variations.changed: the two halves of the scene, joined

mistake.display: Il était tard. Il y avait personne. Alors j'ai appelé Anne
mistake.why: The negative reading needs its ne: Il n'y avait personne.

sentences.usage: Opening an account — the situation first, then what you did about it.
sentences.mnemonic: Imparfait sets the scene. Passé composé moves it.

sentences.display: Je mangeais quand tu as appelé
sentences.cue: I was eating when you called
sentences.literal: I was-eating when you have called

words.note: The imparfait of L1-M3's manger. The e before the a keeps the g soft — mangeais, not mangais.
It glues the two tenses together: background before it, event after it. It also asks a question — Quand est-ce que tu es rentré?
The participle of arriver. Movement, so être and agreement — il est arrivé, elle est arrivée.

sentences.trap: The eating and the call took the same kind of time. What separates them is that one is scenery and the other is the event — a decision about the telling rather than about the world.
sentences.sound: zhuh mon-ZHAY kon tü a a-puh-LAY. The an of quand is nasal.

variations.display: Je travaillais quand tu as appelé
variations.cue: I was working when you called
variations.changed: a different background

variations.display: Je mangeais quand il est arrivé
variations.cue: I was eating when he arrived
variations.changed: an arrival, so être and agreement

variations.display: Hier j'ai mangé à sept heures
variations.cue: Yesterday I ate at seven
variations.changed: a completed step — the same verb, the other tense

mistake.display: J'ai mangé quand tu as appelé
mistake.why: The background clause is imparfait: Je mangeais quand tu as appelé.

sentences.usage: Explaining what you were in the middle of.

sentences.display: Hier il pleuvait. Je suis resté à la maison
sentences.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I stayed at home
sentences.literal: Yesterday it was-raining. I am stayed at the house

words.note: The imparfait of L1-M9's il pleut. Weather is almost always imparfait in an account, because it is the scenery rather than an event.
The imparfait of L1-M1's travailler. Every -er verb takes the same -ais, -ait, -ions endings, so the class is regular throughout.

sentences.trap: rester takes être even though nothing moves. The law is "movement and change of state", and French counts staying put as the second — a place the rule has to be learnt rather than reasoned out.
sentences.sound: eel pluh-VAY. zhuh swee res-TAY. The eu of pleuvait is the rounded vowel.

variations.display: Hier il pleuvait. Je suis restée à la maison
variations.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I stayed at home
variations.changed: said by a woman, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Il faisait froid. Je suis resté à la maison
variations.cue: It was cold. I stayed at home
variations.changed: a different kind of weather

variations.display: Hier il pleuvait. J'ai pris le bus
variations.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I took the bus
variations.changed: avoir, and no agreement at all

mistake.display: Hier il pleuvait. J'ai resté à la maison
mistake.why: rester takes être: Je suis resté à la maison.

sentences.usage: Explaining a day that did not go to plan.

sentences.display: Il faisait froid et je n'avais pas ma clé
sentences.cue: It was cold and I didn't have my key
sentences.literal: It was-making cold and I not-had not my key

words.note: French MAKES weather rather than being it: il fait froid, il faisait chaud. L1-M9's own idiom, in the imparfait — and chaud is its other half.
The imparfait of avoir. Having something is a state rather than an event, so it is nearly always this tense. Negated it elides: je n'avais pas.

sentences.trap: Both halves are imparfait because neither is a step. Nothing has happened yet in this sentence — it is entirely scene-setting, and the account has not started to move.
sentences.sound: eel fuh-ZAY FRWA ay zhuh na-VAY pa ma KLAY. The ai of faisait is said uh, unusually.

variations.display: Il faisait chaud et je n'avais pas d'eau
variations.cue: It was hot and I had no water
variations.changed: the opposite weather, and M5's negated partitive

variations.display: Il faisait froid. Je suis rentré
variations.cue: It was cold. I went home
variations.changed: with a step after the scene

variations.display: Je n'avais pas ma clé
variations.cue: I didn't have my key
variations.changed: the second half alone

mistake.display: Il était froid et je n'avais pas ma clé
mistake.why: Weather is made, not been: Il faisait froid.

sentences.usage: Setting up a story that is about to go wrong.

sentences.display: D'abord j'ai mangé, ensuite je suis sorti
sentences.cue: First I ate, then I went out
sentences.literal: At-first I-have eaten, next I am gone-out

words.note: An elision, so one index key. It opens an account, and ensuite and enfin follow it.
A step after the first one. L1-M10's puis does the same job and is shorter; ensuite is the one that pairs with d'abord.
The participle of sortir, and movement, so être and agreement. A woman says je suis sortie.

sentences.trap: One sentence, two auxiliaries: ai with manger and suis with sortir. Nothing about the meaning of the two events differs — only whether the verb involves movement.
sentences.sound: da-BOR zhay mon-ZHAY on-SWEET zhuh swee sor-TEE. The apostrophe of d'abord is a join.

variations.display: D'abord j'ai mangé, ensuite je suis sortie
variations.cue: First I ate, then I went out
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.display: D'abord je suis sorti, ensuite j'ai mangé
variations.cue: First I went out, then I ate
variations.changed: the order swapped, and the auxiliaries with it

variations.display: J'ai mangé, puis je suis sorti
variations.cue: I ate, then I went out
variations.changed: L1-M10's shorter sequencer

mistake.display: D'abord j'ai mangé, ensuite j'ai sorti
mistake.why: Movement takes être: ensuite je suis sorti.

sentences.usage: Telling someone the order things happened in.

sentences.display: J'ai perdu mon billet. Enfin j'ai pris le bus
sentences.cue: I lost my ticket. In the end I took the bus
sentences.literal: I-have lost my ticket. Finally I-have taken the bus

words.note: It closes an account and marks the last step rather than merely the latest. The in is nasal and no n is said.
The participle of prendre. With avoir it does not agree, and its shape has to be learnt — it is nothing like the infinitive.

sentences.trap: Both verbs take avoir and neither participle agrees. That is the easy half of the law — with avoir nothing on the end ever moves.
sentences.sound: on-FAN zhay pree luh BÜSS. The s of pris is silent.

variations.display: J'ai perdu mon billet. Enfin je suis rentré
variations.cue: I lost my ticket. In the end I went home
variations.changed: movement in the second half, so être

variations.display: Enfin j'ai pris le bus
variations.cue: In the end I took the bus
variations.changed: the second half alone

variations.display: J'ai perdu mon billet. Puis j'ai pris le bus
variations.cue: I lost my ticket. Then I took the bus
variations.changed: puis rather than enfin — a step, not the last one

mistake.display: J'ai perdu mon billet. Enfin j'ai prise le bus
mistake.why: With avoir the participle does not agree: j'ai pris le bus.

sentences.usage: The story of a journey that went wrong and then worked out.

sentences.display: Il y avait beaucoup de monde. Alors je suis rentré
sentences.cue: There were a lot of people. So I went home
sentences.literal: It there had much of world. So I am returned

words.note: beaucoup de monde is "a lot of people", and the word literally means world. It is singular, so nothing around it goes plural.
L1-M9's rentrer. Movement, so être and agreement — je suis rentré for a man, rentrée for a woman.

sentences.trap: monde is singular and "people" is plural. Translating the English number would put a plural verb where French wants a singular one.
sentences.sound: eel nya-VAY bo-KOO duh MOND. The p of beaucoup is silent.

variations.display: Il y avait beaucoup de monde. Alors je suis rentrée
variations.cue: There were a lot of people. So I went home
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.display: Il n'y avait pas beaucoup de monde
variations.cue: There weren't many people
variations.changed: negated

variations.display: Il y avait beaucoup de monde au cinéma
variations.cue: There were a lot of people at the cinema
variations.changed: with a place

mistake.display: Il y avaient beaucoup de monde. Alors je suis rentré
mistake.why: il y avait never changes: Il y avait beaucoup de monde.

sentences.usage: Describing a place that was crowded, and what you did about it.

sentences.display: Quand j'étais petit, j'allais toujours à la mer
sentences.cue: When I was little, I always went to the seaside
sentences.literal: When I-was little, I-was-going always to the sea

words.note: The je and tu cells of the imparfait of être, spelled the same. Before a vowel je elides onto it: j'étais.
A habit, so the imparfait — and a habit is not a duration. English needs "used to" here and French needs only the tense. Its participle allé agrees, because aller is movement.
à la mer is the seaside as a place to go. It is feminine, and it sounds exactly like mère, M2's mother.
Two jobs on one word: always in a habit, still in the present. The final s is silent and the word never changes.

sentences.trap: Nothing here is ongoing and nothing is background. It is a habit, which is the third job the imparfait does — and the one that most clearly breaks the "ongoing" slogan.
sentences.sound: kon zhay-TAY puh-TEE zha-LAY too-ZHOOR a la MEHR. mer and mère are homophones.

variations.display: Quand j'étais petite, j'allais toujours à la mer
variations.cue: When I was little, I always went to the seaside
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.display: Quand j'étais petit, je mangeais à la maison
variations.cue: When I was little, I ate at home
variations.changed: a different habit

variations.display: J'allais toujours à la mer
variations.cue: I always used to go to the seaside
variations.changed: without saying when

mistake.display: Quand j'étais petit, je suis toujours allé à la mer
mistake.why: A habit takes the imparfait: j'allais toujours à la mer.

sentences.usage: Talking about childhood, which is where the imparfait lives.
sentences.mnemonic: A habit is not a duration.

sentences.display: Il était tard. J'ai appelé Anne. Enfin nous sommes sortis
sentences.cue: It was late. I called Anne. In the end we went out
sentences.literal: It was late. I-have called Anne. Finally we are gone-out

words.note: The nous cell of être, and here it is the auxiliary. L1-M10 showed nous sommes allés without opening the word itself.
The third-person cell of avais. The whole imparfait of avoir is regular, unlike its present.

sentences.trap: Three sentences, one scene and two steps. The scene is imparfait and both steps are passé composé — and the second takes être because going out is movement, so its participle counts us.
sentences.sound: on-FAN noo som sor-TEE. The s of sortis is silent and the agreement is invisible.

variations.display: Il était tard. J'ai appelé Anne
variations.cue: It was late. I called Anne
variations.changed: two sentences instead of three

variations.display: J'étais fatigué. Enfin je suis rentré
variations.cue: I was tired. In the end I went home
variations.changed: a different scene and a different ending

variations.display: Enfin nous sommes sortis ensemble
variations.cue: In the end we went out together
variations.changed: with M6's word on the end

mistake.display: Il était tard. J'ai appelé Anne. Enfin nous avons sortis
mistake.why: Movement takes être: nous sommes sortis.

sentences.usage: A whole small account — a situation, a step, an outcome.

sentences.display: Hier il faisait chaud. Nous sommes allés à la mer. Enfin j'ai dormi
sentences.cue: Yesterday it was hot. We went to the seaside. In the end I slept
sentences.literal: Yesterday it was-making hot. We are gone to the sea. Finally I-have slept

words.note: The participle of L1-M6's dormir. Sleeping is neither movement nor a change of state, so it takes avoir and does not agree.

sentences.trap: Three verbs, three different tenses or auxiliaries, and each is chosen by the rule rather than by the meaning: weather is scenery, going is movement, sleeping is neither.
sentences.sound: eel fuh-ZAY SHO. noo som a-LAY a la MEHR. The participle allés agrees with a plural we and no s is heard.

variations.display: Hier il faisait chaud. Nous sommes allés à la mer
variations.cue: Yesterday it was hot. We went to the seaside
variations.changed: two sentences

variations.display: Il faisait chaud. Je suis allé à la mer
variations.cue: It was hot. I went to the seaside
variations.changed: one person, so the participle agrees with him

variations.display: J'étais fatigué. Enfin j'ai dormi
variations.cue: I was tired. In the end I slept
variations.changed: a different scene, and avoir on the last verb

mistake.display: Hier il faisait chaud. Nous avons allés à la mer. Enfin j'ai dormi
mistake.why: Movement takes être: Nous sommes allés à la mer.

sentences.usage: A whole day told in three sentences, which is what an account is.
sentences.mnemonic: The rule picks the auxiliary, not the meaning.
